**West Lake**, also known as **Xihu** and by [other names](#Names), is a [freshwater lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freshwater_lake "Freshwater lake") in [Hangzhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou "Hangzhou"), [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"). Situated to the west of Hangzhou's former [walled city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_City_Walls "Hangzhou City Walls"), the lake has a surface area of
evidence.title: West Lake - Wikipedia

evidence.text:
6.39 km2 (2.47 sq mi),[[1]](#cite_note-:0-1) stretching 3.2 km (2.0 mi) from north to south and 2.8 km (1.7 mi) from east to west.[[2]](#cite_note-:26-2) In the lake are four [causeways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Causeway "Causeway"), three [artificial islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_island "Artificial island"), and Gushan, the only natural island.[[1]](#cite_note-:0-1) Gentle hills surround the lake on its north, west, and south sides,[[3]](#cite_note-:14-3) with the [Leifeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leifeng_Pagoda "Leifeng Pagoda") and [Baochu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baochu_Pagoda "Baochu Pagoda") pagodas standing in pair on the south and north banks.[[4]](#cite_note-monuments-4) Several famous temples are nestled in the mountains west of the lake, including [Lingyin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingyin_Temple "Lingyin Temple") and [Jingci Temples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jingci_Temple "Jingci Temple").[[4]](#cite_note-monuments-4)

A tourist attraction since the [Tang dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tang_dynasty "Tang dynasty") (618–907),[[5]](#cite_note-intro-5) the lake has influenced [poets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_poetry "Chinese poetry") and [painters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_painting "Chinese painting") throughout [Chinese history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_China "History of China") for its natural beauty and historic relics.[[6]](#cite_note-:27-6) By the [Song dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_dynasty "Song dynasty") (960–1279), during which the [dynastic capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_capitals_of_China "Historical capitals of China") moved to Hangzhou, it had become a cultural landmark and one of the most visited tourist destinations of China.[[5]](#cite_note-intro-5) Introduced to Europeans by [Marco Polo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Polo "Marco Polo"), the lake was once a symbol of Chinese urban culture.[[5]](#cite_note-intro-5) It has been featured on [Chinese currency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renminbi "Renminbi"), including the one-yuan [banknote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banknote "Banknote") in the 1979 [Bank of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_China "Bank of China") [Foreign Exchange Certificate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_exchange_certificate "Foreign exchange certificate")[[7]](#cite_note-:28-7) and the [2005 Renminbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_series_of_the_renminbi "Fifth series of the renminbi"),[[8]](#cite_note-:29-8) as well as in the [Chinese passport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_passport "Chinese passport").[[9]](#cite_note-:30-9) A [UNESCO World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site") since 2011, the lake is recognised to have influenced garden designs in China, [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan"), and [Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korea "Korea") over the centuries as "an idealised fusion between humans and nature."[[10]](#cite_note-whc-10)

The lake, along with the surrounding hills, constitutes the **West Lake Scenic Area**, which is governed by the [Management Committee of Hangzhou West Lake Scenic Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Management_Committee_of_Hangzhou_West_Lake_Scenic_Area "Management Committee of Hangzhou West Lake Scenic Area"), a special administration dedicated to cultural preservation and gardening under the Hangzhou municipal government since 2002.[[11]](#cite_note-11) The first major Chinese tourist attraction to cancel admission fees,[[12]](#cite_note-:20-12) the scenic area is crowded during public holidays.[[13]](#cite_note-13) Over the 2024 [National Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Day_of_the_People's_Republic_of_China "National Day of the People's Republic of China") holiday, the area received 4.426 million visitors in seven days, a 30.92% rise from the previous year.[[14]](#cite_note-:21-14)

## Names

[[e
evidence.title: West Lake - Wikipedia

evidence.text:
dit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Names")]

Historically, the lake has been referred to by various names, including **Qiantang Lake**.[[15]](#cite_note-names-15) The first description of the waters near Hangzhou was made in the *[Book of Han](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_of_Han "Book of Han")* finished in 111, which states,[[16]](#cite_note-:7-16)

> The Western Commandery Captain of Qiantang was stationed at the Wulin Hills, where the Wulin River originates. The river flows eastward into the sea, covering a distance of 830 li [350 km; 220 mi].

This statement about the Wulin River (武林水) is widely interpreted as the first mention of West Lake, while the Wulin Hills (武林山) are believed to be the hills near the [Lingyin Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingyin_Temple "Lingyin Temple").[[16]](#cite_note-:7-16)

[Bai Juyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bai_Juyi "Bai Juyi") was among the first to refer to the lake as "West Lake", due to its location to the west of the city.[[5]](#cite_note-intro-5) [Su Shi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Su_Shi "Su Shi") was the first to use the name in official documents, in his request to the [Imperial Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_dynasty "Song dynasty") for the dredging of the lake in 1090.[[17]](#cite_note-17) 16th-century Chinese scholars considered the West Lake of Hangzhou to be the most famous among the 35 other lakes with the same name in China.[[18]](#cite_note-:5-18) In English, the name has also been variously translated and [romanized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanization_of_Chinese "Romanization of Chinese") as **the West Lake**,[[19]](#cite_note-19) the **Western Lake**,[[20]](#cite_note-eb9-20) **Si-hu**,[[21]](#cite_note-eb11-21) **Hsi Hu**,[[22]](#cite_note-22) **Xi Hu**,[[6]](#cite_note-:27-6) **Lake Si**,[[23]](#cite_note-23) **Lake Hsi**,[[24]](#cite_note-24) **Lake Hsi-hu**,[[25]](#cite_note-25) and **Xi Lake**.[[2]](#cite_note-:26-2) Due to Su Shi's famous comparison with [Xizi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Shi "Xi Shi"), the lake is also sometimes described in Chinese as Xizi Lake.[[5]](#cite_note-intro-5)

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

### Natural formation and dredging efforts

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Natural formation and dredging efforts")]

About 4,400 to 2,500 years ago, as sea levels fell, the [Hangzhou-Jiaxing-Huzhou plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou–Jiaxing–Huzhou_Plain "Hangzhou–Jiaxing–Huzhou Plain") began to emerge, while West Lake was merely a shallow bay. Over time, the [Qiantang River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qiantang_River "Qiantang River") gradually deposited sand and rocks outside this bay. About 2,000 years ago, a lagoon was formed. Streams from the surrounding mountains transformed the water into freshwater, but ongoing silt deposits gradually reduced the lake to a swamp.[[26]](#cite_note-:10-26) In local [folklore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folklore "Folklore"), when [Qin Shi Huang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qin_Shi_Huang "Qin Shi Huang") (259–210 BC), the first [emperor of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_of_China "Emperor of China"), visited Hangzhou, West Lake was still part of the Qiantang River. The giant rock on the north bank of West Lake was said to be where the emperor anchored his fleet. According to *[Records of the Grand Historian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiji "Shiji")*, during his visit in 210 BC, the emperor was halted in Hangzhou by the strong tide of the Qiantang River and had to take a detour westward to reach Shaoxing.[[27]](#cite_note-27) During the Eastern Han era (25–220), local official Hua Xin ordered the construction of a seawall to completely cut the lake off from the sea.[[28]](#cite_note-28)[[29]](#cite_note-29) In 591, the government seat of Hangzhou, originally on the west shore, was relocated to t
evidence.title: West Lake - Wikipedia

evidence.text:
he newly built walled city east of the lake. With the completion of the [Grand Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Canal_(China) "Grand Canal (China)"), Hangzhou, as its destination, became a transport hub of China.[[30]](#cite_note-30)

|  |
| --- |
| "The lovely Spring breeze has come Back to the Lake of the West. The Spring waters are so clear and Green they might be freshly painted. The clouds of perfume are sweeter Than can be imagined. In the Gentle East wind the petals Fall like grains of rice." |
| —[Ouyang Xiu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ouyang_Xiu "Ouyang Xiu") (1007–1072), excerpts from *Spring Day on West Lake*[[31]](#cite_note-31) |

Before the [Tang dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tang_dynasty "Tang dynasty") (618–907), West Lake was a shallow body of water,[[32]](#cite_note-32) but continuous dredging efforts prevented it from becoming a swamp.[[33]](#cite_note-33) During the Jianzhong period (780–783) of the [Tang dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tang_dynasty "Tang dynasty"), local official [Li Bi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Bi "Li Bi") diverted water[*[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")*] into Hangzhou via underground pipes, creating six ponds to secure the city's water supply. In 822, [Bai Juyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bai_Juyi "Bai Juyi") dredged West Lake and used the silt to build a long causeway between Qiantang and Yuhang Gates, which was named in his memory. Under the [Wuyue Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuyue "Wuyue") (907–932), with Hangzhou being the capital, King Qian Liu ordered annual dredging of West Lake with soldiers to maintain water quality for water supply. In the Song dynasty, [Su Shi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Su_Shi "Su Shi") (1037–1101) ordered the construction of the Su Causeway from dredged silt in 1089. He designated an area of the lake with three stone pagodas to prevent water chestnut planting and reduce silting, which may mark the origin of the "Three Ponds Mirroring the Moon."[[34]](#cite_note-:1-34) By 1275, military patrols were appointed to maintain and police the lake, where littering of any rubbish or planting additional lotuses or water-chestnuts were forbidden.[[35]](#cite_note-:8-35)

### From literary tradition to tourism

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: From literary tradition to tourism")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/%E5%85%83%E8%B6%99%E5%AD%9F%E9%A0%AB%E6%9B%B8%E8%98%87%E8%BB%BE%E8%A5%BF%E6%B9%96%E8%A9%A9PAD.jpg/250px-%E5%85%83%E8%B6%99%E5%AD%9F%E9%A0%AB%E6%9B%B8%E8%98%87%E8%BB%BE%E8%A5%BF%E6%B9%96%E8%A9%A9PAD.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:元趙孟頫書蘇軾西湖詩PAD.jpg)

*Su Shi's Verse on West Lake* by Zhao Mengfu in 1320

Literary works by renowned literati contributed to the fame of Hangzhou's West Lake among Chinese intellectuals.[[5]](#cite_note-intro-5) Especially, the lake became associated with the two greatest poets of Middle-Period China, Bai Juyi and Su Shi.[[35]](#cite_note-:8-35): 51–52 [Su Xiaoxiao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Su_Xiaoxiao "Su Xiaoxiao"), a famous courtesan and poet of [Southern Qi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Qi "Southern Qi") (479–502), was buried upon West Lake. Her life and poetry have inspired later poets, including [Li He](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_He "Li He") and [Wen Tingyun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wen_Tingyun "Wen Tingyun"). Over time, local history became intertwined with the natural beauty. For example, [Bai Juyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bai_Juyi "Bai Juyi") celebrates Su Xiaoxiao's beauty and her connection to the enchanting scenery of the lake in one of his poem. When [Su Shi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Su_Shi "Su Shi") (1037–1101) famously compared West Lake to [Xizi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Shi "Xi Shi"), one of the [Four Beaut
evidence.title: West Lake - Wikipedia

evidence.text:
ies of ancient China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Beauties "Four Beauties"), the lake also became known as the Xizi Lake:[[5]](#cite_note-intro-5)

> 水光瀲灧睛方好，  
>  山色空濛雨亦奇。  
>  欲把西湖比西子，  
>  淡妝濃抹總相宜。

Translation:
> The shimmering water shines in clear light,  
>  While misty mountains bring rain's charm to sight.  
>  If West Lake I liken to Xizi fair,  
>  Both light and heavy makeup suits her well.

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/West_Lake_by_Tomita_Keisen%2C_1909%2C_six-panel_screen%2C_Honolulu_Museum_of_Art.jpg/250px-West_Lake_by_Tomita_Keisen%2C_1909%2C_six-panel_screen%2C_Honolulu_Museum_of_Art.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:West_Lake_by_Tomita_Keisen,_1909,_six-panel_screen,_Honolulu_Museum_of_Art.jpg)

*West Lake* by Japanese painter [Tomita Keisen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomita_Keisen "Tomita Keisen") (1909), with a tribute to [Bai Juyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bai_Juyi "Bai Juyi") in the writing

During the period of [Wuyue Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuyue_Kingdom "Wuyue Kingdom") (907–978), numerous temples, pagodas, shrines, and grottoes were built or expanded around the lake, including Lingyin, Zhaoqing, Jingci, Li’an, Liutong, and Taoguang temples, as well as the Baochu, Liuhe, Leifeng, and White pagodas, due to the devotion of its rulers to Buddhism.[[26]](#cite_note-:10-26) Since the 12th and 13th centuries, these temples, frequently visited by Japanese monks, played a significant role in circulating cultural images of the lake across East Asia, as these visitors returned to their home countries.[[36]](#cite_note-36)

Wars and conflicts in northern China during the Song dynasty—including invasions by the [Khitan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khitan_people "Khitan people"), [Jurchen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurchen_people "Jurchen people"), and [Mongols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongols "Mongols")—triggered significant migration southward to the new capital, leading to urbanisation and economic prosperity. With city walls blocking much of the natural scenery, West Lake became a favoured destination for urban residents seeking respite from the demands of city life and political turmoil.[[5]](#cite_note-intro-5) In 1129, the capital of the Song dynasty was relocated to Hangzhou, after the country lost its northern territories to the Jurchen. The [imperial examination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_examination "Imperial examination") held every three years filled Hangzhou with educated individuals, who often enjoyed the lake's beauty and consulted fortune-tellers at lakeside temples. Visiting West Lake inspired poems that reflected on their experiences and memories of the scenery.[[37]](#cite_note-writing-37)

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/Scenic_Attractions_of_West_Lake_%E8%A5%BF%E6%B9%96%E6%B8%85%E8%B6%A3%E5%9C%96_%2811%29.jpg/250px-Scenic_Attractions_of_West_Lake_%E8%A5%BF%E6%B9%96%E6%B8%85%E8%B6%A3%E5%9C%96_%2811%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Scenic_Attractions_of_West_Lake_西湖清趣圖_(11).jpg)

*Scenic Attractions of West Lake* (c. 14th century)

By the late Song dynasty, West Lake had evolved into a significant hub where tourism emerged. While [pilgrimage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pilgrimage "Pilgrimage") and contemplative retreat had previously been the main motives for travel, sightseeing gained wide acceptance as an activity focused on enjoyment and the appreciation of natural beauty, roughly at the same time as in western Europe.[[38]](#cite_note-38) Aesthetic appreciation of landscapes became a popular business, with diverse entertainment options which involved standardised routes and viewing orders made available to cater to various preferences and budgets. Tour guides, seasonal markets and specialty shops emerged.[[5]](#cite_note-intro-5
evidence.title: West Lake - Wikipedia

evidence.text:
) The notion of [Ten Scenes of West Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten_Scenes_of_West_Lake "Ten Scenes of West Lake") was invented.[[39]](#cite_note-:3-39) Boating on the lake was a popular pastime, with records noting hundreds of intricately carved, elegantly decorated boats gliding gracefully over the water.[[5]](#cite_note-intro-5)

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/China_Hangzhou_Westlake-2.jpg/250px-China_Hangzhou_Westlake-2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:China_Hangzhou_Westlake-2.jpg)

Decorated boats on the lake

Shortly after the [Mongol conquest of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongol_conquest_of_China "Mongol conquest of China"), West Lake remained socially vibrant. The official records show that in 1309, the city received more than 1,200 foreign visitors within half a year, many from Turkestan and Europe. West Lake was dredged and renamed the “Pond of Freeing Captive Animals” under [Kublai Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kublai_Khan "Kublai Khan"), while parts of the lake area were gradually cultivated into farmland. Among the visitors was [Marco Polo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Polo "Marco Polo"), who describes the lake in his book,[[40]](#cite_note-40)

> Inside the city there is a Lake which has a compass of some 30 miles: and all round it are erected beautiful palaces and mansions, of the richest and most exquisite structure that you can imagine, belonging to the nobles of the city. There are also on its shores many abbeys and churches of the Idolaters. In the middle of the Lake are two Islands, on each of which stands a rich, beautiful and spacious edifice, furnished in such style as to seem fit for the palace of an Emperor.

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/Yu_Fei_Temple.jpg/330px-Yu_Fei_Temple.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yu_Fei_Temple.jpg)

[Yue Fei Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yue_Fei_Temple "Yue Fei Temple")

### Mongol rule and fall of tourism

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Mongol rule and fall of tourism")]

The booming tourism led to different interpretations. The lake was regarded as a literary tradition, a symbol of the state and a part of local history and knowledge, but for some, a symbol of extravagance and luxury.[[37]](#cite_note-writing-37) One of the most famous portrayal comes from Lin Sheng, who penned a poem as a satirical commentary on how people were engrossed in their indulgence in Hangzhou's pleasures, rather than making efforts to reclaim the lost northern capital:[[41]](#cite_note-epilogue-41)

 

> 山外青山樓外樓，  
>  西湖歌舞幾時休？  
>  暖風熏得遊人醉，  
>  直把杭州作汴州。

Translation:
> Beyond the hills, more hills rise, beyond the pavilions, more pavilions stand.  
>  When will the songs and dances on West Lake finally end?  
>  The warm breeze intoxicates the travellers,  
>  Making them mistake Hangzhou for Bianzhou.

In 1142, Yue Fei, a hawkish Chinese general known for his determined efforts to reclaim northern China, was executed by the dovish emperor and his chief councillor.[[39]](#cite_note-:3-39)[[42]](#cite_note-:9-42) Yue's death marked the end of attempts to recapture the north, as the emperor prioritised peace despite the Song army's successes.[[42]](#cite_note-:9-42) Yue Fei remained widely admired among Chinese people and was widely celebrated as a national hero.[[43]](#cite_note-43) In 1162, his wrongful execution was acknowledged, and his remains were moved to a tomb by West Lake. Since 1221, a nearby temple has been repurposed in his memory.[[4]](#cite_note-monuments-4)

The Mongol-led [Yuan dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuan_dynasty "Yuan dynasty") (1271–1368) saw the decline of tourism at West Lake.[[41]](#cite_note-epilogue-41) Government support for maintaining the lake diminished, as Mongol rule
evidence.title: West Lake - Wikipedia

evidence.text:
rs placed their political and economic focus on northern China rather than the south.[[41]](#cite_note-epilogue-41) The Mongol rulers, as well as local residents, blamed the lavish life upon the lake for the fall of Song. Therefore, the lake was abandoned.[[41]](#cite_note-epilogue-41)[[44]](#cite_note-dredging-44) When the Ming dynasty replaced Mongol rule, Hangzhou gradually regained its prosperity by the mid-15th century. However, the lake experienced droughts in 1442 and 1456, causing it to dry up temporarily.[[39]](#cite_note-:3-39)

### Revitalisation in Late Imperial China

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Revitalisation in Late Imperial China")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/%E8%A5%BF%E6%B9%96._%E6%9D%A8%E5%85%AC%E5%A0%A4_-_panoramio.jpg/250px-%E8%A5%BF%E6%B9%96._%E6%9D%A8%E5%85%AC%E5%A0%A4_-_panoramio.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:西湖._杨公堤_-_panoramio.jpg)

Yanggong Causeway (est. 1508)

Since the mid-Ming era, renewed dredging projects rekindled public interest in West Lake. As Hangzhou developed as a publishing centre, the production of geographic texts stimulated tourism, which in turn further fuelled the publishing industry.[[45]](#cite_note-:6-45) In 1508, Hangzhou governor Yang Mengying led a major dredging effort, repairing the Su and Bai Causeways and creating the Yanggong Causeway in his memory. This restoration returned the lake's appearance to its Tang dynasty splendour. Further construction works in 1576, 1607-1611 and 1621 built the Mid-Lake Pavilion and the Lesser Yingzhou Islet.[[46]](#cite_note-:15-46) The period of time saw the publication of a series of books on local history and culture which depicted West Lake, inspiring Japanese gardens such as the [Kyū Shiba Rikyū Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyū_Shiba_Rikyū_Garden "Kyū Shiba Rikyū Garden").[[46]](#cite_note-:15-46)

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/%E6%B8%85%E8%91%A3%E9%82%A6%E9%81%94%E8%A5%BF%E6%B9%96%E5%8D%81%E6%99%AF_%E5%8D%B74.png/250px-%E6%B8%85%E8%91%A3%E9%82%A6%E9%81%94%E8%A5%BF%E6%B9%96%E5%8D%81%E6%99%AF_%E5%8D%B74.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:清董邦達西湖十景_卷4.png)

*Ten Scenic Spots of West Lake* (mid-18th century)

The [Manchu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchu_people "Manchu people") conquered Hangzhou in 1645, which led to the construction of residences alongside the lake.[[39]](#cite_note-:3-39) During the [High Qing era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Qing_era "High Qing era") (1683–1799), emperors frequented southern China, to symbolise their control.[[39]](#cite_note-:3-39) Due to the visits by the Qing emperors, the lake was fully dredged and renovated.[[26]](#cite_note-:10-26) In 1689, a temporary imperial palace was built on Gushan.[[26]](#cite_note-:10-26) In 1722, Zhejiang governor Li Wei was ordered to dredge the lake.[[39]](#cite_note-:3-39) In 1809, Ruan Gong Islet was built with silted soil, which was named after Ruan Yuan, then governor of Zhejiang.[[46]](#cite_note-:15-46)

The emperors revived and standardised the notion of the Ten Scenes of West Lake. The Kangxi Emperor inscribed titles for these scenes, which were later carved into stelae beneath ten pavilions. The Qianlong Emperor composed poems during his visits, which were then inscribed on the reverse side of Kangxi's stelae. He further inscribed the Eight Scenes of Dragon Well in the surrounding hills. In Beijing, imperial gardens, including the Garden of Delighted Spring and the [Old Summer Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Summer_Palace "Old Summer Palace"), were designed to imitate the landscape designs of West Lake.[[39]](#cite_note-:3-39)

After the [Taiping Rebellion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiping_Rebellion "Taiping Rebellion") (1850–1864) destroyed various buildings beside the la
evidence.title: West Lake - Wikipedia

evidence.text:
ke, West Lake revived as major Qing military leaders, magnates, and ranking officials, such as [Peng Yulin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peng_Yulin "Peng Yulin") built their villas upon the lake, which later became their memorial temples and shrines that were later maintained by a dedicated division of local government.[[47]](#cite_note-:16-47) In 1864, the West Lake Dredging Bureau was established, to manage the dredging of the lake.[[26]](#cite_note-:10-26)

### Modern era

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Modern era")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Hangzhou_Wenlan_Pavilion_20161002.jpg/250px-Hangzhou_Wenlan_Pavilion_20161002.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hangzhou_Wenlan_Pavilion_20161002.jpg)

[Wenlan Pavilion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wenlan_Pavilion "Wenlan Pavilion"), an imperial library that became part of [Zhejiang Provincial Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_Provincial_Museum "Zhejiang Provincial Museum") in 1929

Following the [1911 revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xinhai_Revolution "Xinhai Revolution") that ended the Qing dynasty, the Manchu quarter of the city was demolished, including both its separate fortifications and the section of the [city wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_City_Wall "Hangzhou City Wall") that separated it from the lakefront. Qing imperial properties around West Lake were also nationalised.[[39]](#cite_note-:3-39)[[48]](#cite_note-48) Land in the Manchu quarter was sold at auction to establish a New Business District and the lakefront renovated as a string of public parks, integrating West Lake into the new heart of the city.[[49]](#cite_note-49) The former imperial palace on Gushan was converted into Zhongshan Park, named for [Sun Yat-sen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Yat-sen "Sun Yat-sen").[[39]](#cite_note-:3-39) The buildings associated with former Qing officials and generals were renamed after Ming loyalists, as with the Shrine of Former Martyrs.[[47]](#cite_note-:16-47) The [railway link](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai-Hangzhou_Railway "Shanghai-Hangzhou Railway") between Hangzhou and Shanghai, completed in 1909, stimulated local tourism.[[47]](#cite_note-:16-47)

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Chenglu_7186.jpg/250px-Chenglu_7186.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chenglu_7186.jpg)

[Chiang Kai-shek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiang_Kai-shek "Chiang Kai-shek")'s West Lake residence

A great number of lakeside villas and garden were built, and further tombs were forbidden to be built around the lake.[[26]](#cite_note-:10-26) The visitors to the lake included notable literati, such as [Rabindranath Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabindranath_Tagore "Rabindranath Tagore") and [Ryūnosuke Akutagawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryūnosuke_Akutagawa "Ryūnosuke Akutagawa"), as well as the couple of [Chiang Kai-shek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiang_Kai-shek "Chiang Kai-shek") and [Soong Mei-ling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soong_Mei-ling "Soong Mei-ling") spent their honeymoon by the lake.[[39]](#cite_note-:3-39) In 1922, the [Chinese Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party") held the [Hangzhou Plenum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_Plenum?action=edit&redlink=1 "Hangzhou Plenum (page does not exist)") here, initiating the first collaboration with Nationalists.[[39]](#cite_note-:3-39) In 1928, the [National Academy of Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Academy_of_Art "China Academy of Art") was founded on Gushan Island.[[39]](#cite_note-:3-39)

From 6 June to 20 October 1929, the West Lake Exposition was held.[[50]](#cite_note-:210-50): 54 The exposition showcased Chinese merchandise and culture—particularly tho
evidence.title: West Lake - Wikipedia

evidence.text:
se of Hangzhou and [Jiangnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiangnan "Jiangnan")—to a global audience.[[50]](#cite_note-:210-50): 55 The event included patriotic education and the dissemination of political messages through its Revolutionary Memorial Hall, Revolutionary Memorial Tower, and Revolutionary Memorial Hall Library.[[50]](#cite_note-:210-50): 55

In March 1937, [Zhou Enlai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhou_Enlai "Zhou Enlai") and Chiang Kai-shek held a secret meeting at Yanxia Cave near the lake to negotiate a coalition against [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Japan "Empire of Japan") during the [Second Sino-Japanese War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Sino-Japanese_War "Second Sino-Japanese War").[[39]](#cite_note-:3-39)

The Japanese seized Hangzhou in December 1937.[[51]](#cite_note-51)[[52]](#cite_note-52) Under Japanese rule, deforestation of the mountains surrounding West Lake led to rapid silting of the lake from soil erosion, due to a lack of maintenance.[[47]](#cite_note-:16-47) A Japanese shrine was built by the lake in October 1939, intended as a site for celebrations of the [Japanese mid-autumn festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsukimi "Tsukimi") to familiarise the city's Chinese citizens with [Shintoism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shintoism "Shintoism").[[53]](#cite_note-53) With the Japanese surrender in 1945, tourism at West Lake flourished once again, although the city itself faced severe economic challenges due to hyperinflation.[[39]](#cite_note-:3-39)

The Communists took Hangzhou shortly after the Nationalist retreat from the city to preserve West Lake's cultural relics in 1949. In the 1950s, major hydrological works, along with other construction projects, took place, to exemplify socialist achievements.[[54]](#cite_note-:2-54) [Hangzhou Botanical Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_Botanical_Garden "Hangzhou Botanical Garden") and a flower garden was opened on the lake's west shore. The parks of Fish Viewing at the Flower Pond and Orioles Singing in the Willows were constructed. [Lingyin Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingyin_Temple "Lingyin Temple"), [Jingci Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jingci_Temple "Jingci Temple"), Yue-Wang Temple, Three Ponds Mirroring the Moon, Mid-Lake Pavilion and other spots were renovated.

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b8/President_Richard_Nixon_and_Premier_Chou_En-Lai_Greet_a_Young_Girl_While_Visiting_Hang_Chou%27s_%28Hangzhou%29_West_Lake_Park_in_China_-_DPLA_-_40ba5e3479ff1de48c76a4de7ee2c1ca.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Richard_Nixon_and_Premier_Chou_En-Lai_Greet_a_Young_Girl_While_Visiting_Hang_Chou's_(Hangzhou)_West_Lake_Park_in_China_-_DPLA_-_40ba5e3479ff1de48c76a4de7ee2c1ca.jpg)

U.S. President [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") at West Lake in 1972

Since 1953, [Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party "Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party") [Mao Zedong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mao_Zedong "Mao Zedong") stayed periodically at West Lake every year until his [death in 1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_and_state_funeral_of_Mao_Zedong "Death and state funeral of Mao Zedong").[[55]](#cite_note-55)[[56]](#cite_note-56) To ensure his safety, the local government forcibly relocated residents suspected of connections with the [Nationalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuomintang "Kuomintang") to [labour camps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_camp "Labor camp"). Shops near the lake were acquired by the state, and undercover security personnel were stationed at over 100 shops in the area. The tombs of notable figures—including [Wu Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wu_Song "Wu Song"), [Fang La](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fang_La "Fang La"), [Yu

Qian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yu_Qian "Yu Qian"), [Zhang Cangshui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Cangshui?action=edit&redlink=1 "Zhang Cangshui (page does not exist)"), [Su Manshu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Su_Manshu "Su Manshu"), [Su Xiaoxiao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Su_Xiaoxiao "Su Xiaoxiao"), and the [Stuart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Leighton_Stuart "John Leighton Stuart") family—as well as the temples of [Yue Fei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yue_Fei "Yue Fei") and [Wen Tianxiang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wen_Tianxiang "Wen Tianxiang"), were damaged or destroyed.[[57]](#cite_note-57) During the [Cultural Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Revolution "Cultural Revolution") (1966–1976), Liutong Temple and another temple were destroyed. [Chinese Premier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_of_China "Premier of China") [Zhou Enlai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhou_Enlai "Zhou Enlai") ordered the closure of the [Lingyin Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingyin_Temple "Lingyin Temple") to prevent it from being damaged, but repairs were later made to many scenic sites, due to the visits by the exiled [Cambodian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambodia "Cambodia") [prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_of_Cambodia "Prince of Cambodia") [Norodom Sihanouk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norodom_Sihanouk "Norodom Sihanouk") in 1971 and the [American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA "USA") [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") in 1972.[[39]](#cite_note-:3-39)

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Barack_Obama_and_Xi_Jinping_tea_tour_of_the_West_Lake_State_House_grounds_in_Hangzhou.jpg/250px-Barack_Obama_and_Xi_Jinping_tea_tour_of_the_West_Lake_State_House_grounds_in_Hangzhou.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Barack_Obama_and_Xi_Jinping_tea_tour_of_the_West_Lake_State_House_grounds_in_Hangzhou.jpg)

[Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") and [Xi Jinping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Jinping "Xi Jinping") at the [West Lake State House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Lake_State_House?action=edit&redlink=1 "West Lake State House (page does not exist)") in 2016

After 1976, tourism to the lake revitalised. In 1983, the Hangzhou government refurbished temples and pavilions upon the lake. They also expanded Galloping Tiger Spring and established Curved Yard and Lotus Pool in Summer Park. The new site Exploring Plum Blossoms at Ling Peak was introduced, complemented by cultural events at Huanglong Cave and Ruan Gong Islet. In 1984, local media and societies held public vote to select the new "Ten Scenes" of the lake. In 1985, a pump at Zhakou to draw 300,000 cubic meters of water daily, were built to refresh the water in the lake. A sewage interception project, completed in 1981, installed over 17 kilometres of buried tunnels and 10 pumping stations. In 2000, the [West Lake exposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westlake_exposition "Westlake exposition") was relaunched, drawing 1.4 million visitors. In 2002, Leifeng Pagoda was rebuilt where it collapsed in 1924.[[58]](#cite_note-58) During the [2016 G20 Hangzhou summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_G20_Hangzhou_summit "2016 G20 Hangzhou summit") and the [2023 Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Asian_Games "2022 Asian Games"), West Lake State Guest House was where [General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Secretary_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party "General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party") [Xi Jinping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Jinping "Xi Jinping") met with foreign guests, such as [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama")[[59]](#c

## General layout

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: General layout")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/West_Lake_Map.png/250px-West_Lake_Map.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:West_Lake_Map.png)

Map of West Lake

The layout of West Lake features "one hill, two pagodas, three islets, four causeways and five lakes." Among them, ten classic scenic places are collectively known as the "[Ten Scenes of West Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten_Scenes_of_West_Lake "Ten Scenes of West Lake")".

### Gushan

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Gushan")]

Gushan (孤山), literally "Orphan" or "Solitary Island", is the only natural island on West Lake. Connected to the northern shore by Xiling Bridge and Bai Causeway, Gushan and Bai Causeway separate the North Inner Lake from the Outer West Lake. In local folklore, the island is grouped with the Broken Bridge and the Long Bridge as the "Three Oddities of West Lake": the Broken Bridge is not broken, Solitary Island is not solitary, and the Long Bridge is not long. During the Qing dynasty, Gushan became part of a detached palace for emperors visiting Hangzhou. [Wenlan Pavilion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wenlan_Pavilion "Wenlan Pavilion"), the royal library on the island, housed a valuable collection of literary works and rare texts. After the 1911 revolution, the palace grounds were transformed into Zhongshan Park to honor Sun Yat-sen, a key figure in the revolution. The Wenlan Pavilion and other former palace buildings were incorporated into the [Zhejiang Provincial Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_Provincial_Museum "Zhejiang Provincial Museum"), while a new building next to the Pavilion was completed in 1912 to host the [Zhejiang Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_Library "Zhejiang Library").[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

### Two pagodas

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Two pagodas")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bf/Baochu_Pagoda_in_Hangzhou_2019-02_01.jpg/250px-Baochu_Pagoda_in_Hangzhou_2019-02_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Baochu_Pagoda_in_Hangzhou_2019-02_01.jpg)

Baochu Pagoda and Beishan Road

[Leifeng Pagoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leifeng_Pagoda "Leifeng Pagoda") (雷峰塔), originally built in 975, is located on Sunset Hill. According to local tales, it plays a central role in the [legend of the White Snake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_the_White_Snake "Legend of the White Snake"). Leifeng Pagoda was rebuilt in 2002 after the original structure collapsed in 1924, and it remains a popular tourist spot with stunning views of the lake.[[4]](#cite_note-monuments-4)

[Baochu Pagoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baochu_Pagoda "Baochu Pagoda") (保俶塔), built in 963, stands on Precious Stone Hill. Unlike the more elaborate Leifeng Pagoda, Baochu is a slender, simple structure believed to have been built to pray for the safe return of a local official.[[4]](#cite_note-monuments-4)

### Three islets

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Three islets")]

There are three artificial islets on West Lake: Lesser Yingzhou Islet, Mid-Lake Pavilion, and Ruan Gong Islet. Each was constructed during the Ming and Qing dynasties by dredging lake sediment.

* Lesser Yingzhou Islet (小瀛洲), also known as Three Pools Mirroring the Moon, is especially famous for the small stone pagodas that rise from the water around it. During the Mid-Autumn Festival, these pagodas are lit, creating a scene called "Three Pools M
evidence.title: West Lake - Wikipedia

evidence.text:
irroring the Moon", which has become one of the "Ten Scenes of West Lake."
* Mid-Lake or Lake-Heart Pavilion (湖心亭), the smallest of the three, is a pavilion surrounded by the Outer West Lake. It is renowned for [Zhang Dai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Dai "Zhang Dai")'s essay on watching the snow from the pavilion.
* Ruan Gong Islet (阮公墩), constructed in 1800, is named after [Ruan Yuan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruan_Yuan "Ruan Yuan"), who was the Governor of Zhejiang at the time. Currently, the islet is not open to visitors, as it serves as a natural reserve.

### Four causeways

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Four causeways")]

Three major causeways divide West Lake into five sections, which include:[[61]](#cite_note-elements-61)

* Bai Causeway (白堤) – Originally called the White Sand Causeway, it was naturally formed before the [Tang dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tang_dynasty "Tang dynasty") (618–907) and reinforced between 766 and 779. The causeway collapsed during the [Yuan dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuan_dynasty "Yuan dynasty") (1271–1368) and was rebuilt in 1589. By the Qing dynasty (1644–1911), the causeway became known as the Bai Causeway in memory of [Bai Juyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bai_Juyi "Bai Juyi") and by analogy with the Su Causeway.[[34]](#cite_note-:1-34)[[62]](#cite_note-:4-62)
* Su Causeway (苏堤) – Built in 1089 under the direction of Su Shi during his term as [prefect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hang_Prefecture "Hang Prefecture"), this causeway, along with six bridges to allow ferry passages, connects Quyuan on the north shore to Huagang on the south shore. It separates the Inner Lake from the outer West Lake.
* Yanggong Causeway (杨公堤) – Constructed in 1508 by local official [Yang Mengying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yang_Mengying?action=edit&redlink=1 "Yang Mengying (page does not exist)") (楊孟瑛) to mitigate flooding, this causeway features six bridges that facilitate ferry access between the Inner Lake and the Outer Lake.

Additionally, Zhaogong Causeway (赵公堤), also known as the Jinsha Causeway,[[63]](#cite_note-:17-63) was built in 1242, connecting Quyuan to the Su Causeway. It was named after [Zhao Yuchou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhao_Yuchou?action=edit&redlink=1 "Zhao Yuchou (page does not exist)") (趙與𥲅), then [prefect of Lin'an](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin'an_Prefecture "Lin'an Prefecture").

### Five lakes

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Five lakes")]

The current lake, roughly oval in shape, was dredged during past dynasties and spans 3.3 km from north to south, 2.8 km from east to west, with a shoreline circumference of 15 km and a total water area of 5.6 square kilometres. Divided by Gushan Hill, the Su Causeway, and the Bai Causeway, it consists of five distinct water bodies interconnected by bridge arches.[[61]](#cite_note-elements-61)[[63]](#cite_note-:17-63)

* The Main Lake is bordered by Hubin Road to the east, Su Causeway to the west, Nanshan Road to the south, and Bai Causeway to the north.[[63]](#cite_note-:17-63)
* The West Inner Lake lies west of the Su Causeway.[[63]](#cite_note-:17-63)
* The North Inner Lake, also known as the Back Lake or the Inner Lake, extends from Duanqiao Bridge in the east to Xiling Bridge in the west, Gushan Hill to the south, and Beishan Street to the north.[[63]](#cite_note-:17-63)
* Yuehu Lake is located south of Yue Fei's Temple, west of the Su Causeway, and south of the Breeze-ruffled Lotus at Winding Garden. Sources from the Republic of China era identify it as lying north of the Inner Lake, separated by the Zhaogong Causeway. This lake is likely named after Yue Fei's Tomb, though earlier documentation is unavailable.[[63]](#cite_note-:17-63)
* Lesser South Lake lies north of Nanshan Road, west of the Su Causeway, and south of the Viewing Fish at Flowery Pond sight. Republican-era records describe it as situated

west of Yinbo Bridge and south of Guanyu Pavilion.[[63]](#cite_note-:17-63)

### Ten scenes

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Ten scenes")]

Main article: [Ten Scenes of West Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten_Scenes_of_West_Lake "Ten Scenes of West Lake")

Traditionally, there are ten classic scenic spots on West Lake, each remembered by a [four-character epithet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chengyu "Chengyu"). Collectively, they are known as the Ten Scenes of West Lake, of which the rating dates back to the Song dynasty. Each is marked by a [stele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stele "Stele") with an epithet written in the calligraphy of the [Qianlong Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qianlong_Emperor "Qianlong Emperor").[[64]](#cite_note-:02-64) The ten scenes include:[[65]](#cite_note-:42-65)

## Architecture

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Architecture")]

### Temples and monasteries

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Temples and monasteries")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Lingyin_Temple%2C_Hangzhou_20161003.jpg/250px-Lingyin_Temple%2C_Hangzhou_20161003.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lingyin_Temple,_Hangzhou_20161003.jpg)

[Lingyin Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingyin_Temple "Lingyin Temple")

Buddhism's roots around West Lake extend back to the 4th century with the establishment of [Lingyin Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingyin_Temple "Lingyin Temple") and Tianzhu Temple. During the Five Dynasties period (907–960), the Wuyue rulers, who were devoted Buddhists, initiated extensive temple construction in the region. Notable temples from this period include Jingci Temple on Nanping Hill, Yunqi Temple in Fan Village, and Shangtianzhu Temple on Tianzhu Hill. In addition to these temples, pagodas such as Liuhe, Leifeng, and Baochu were erected, along with intricate stone Buddhist carvings in Yanxia Cave, Shiwu Cave, and on Feilaifeng Peak. During the Song Dynasty, Lingyin Temple and Jingci Temple gained recognition as two of the "Five Mountains and Ten Temples." Across the West Lake Scenic Area, there are 30 Buddhist sites officially designated as protected heritage sites.[[4]](#cite_note-monuments-4) The Baopu Taoist Monastery, rebuilt in the 17th century, enshrines Ge Hong, a prominent Taoist scholar, alchemist, and medical scientist, who conducted Taoist practices and alchemical experiments on Geling Ridge near West Lake.[[4]](#cite_note-monuments-4)

### Tombs and memorial halls

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Tombs and memorial halls")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/20100326_Tombs_of_Yue_Fei_and_Yue_Yun.jpg/250px-20100326_Tombs_of_Yue_Fei_and_Yue_Yun.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:20100326_Tombs_of_Yue_Fei_and_Yue_Yun.jpg)

Tombs of Yue Fei and Yue Yun

Yue Fei's Tomb and Temple serve as a memorial to Yue Fei, a legendary figure in Chinese history known for his loyalty and filial piety. Built in 1163, the tomb honours Yue Fei as a national hero and epitomises the Confucian values that have deeply influenced Chinese society for centuries.[[4]](#cite_note-monuments-4) Tomb of [Su Xiao Xiao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Su_Xiao_Xiao "Su Xiao Xiao") is located near the Xiling Bridge on West Lake's north bank.

### Pavilions and monuments

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Pavilions and monuments")]

Wenlan Pavilion, built in 1784 and rebuilt in 1880, was the only one that exists library among the four libraries commissioned by the Qing imperial family for the collection of *[The Complete Library of the Four Treasuries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siku_Quanshu "Siku Quanshu")*.[[4]](#cite_note-monuments-4)

### Gardens and parks

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Gardens and parks")]

[Xizi Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xizi_Hotel?action=edit&redlink=1 "Xizi Hotel (page does not exist)")

The northeastern shore of West Lake features Hubin Park, a series of six connected parks along the lakefront, surrounded by upscale shopping centers and hotels. At Park No. 3, visitors can enjoy a musical fountain with free performances every evening. To the northwest, [Hangzhou Flower Nursery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_Flower_Nursery?action=edit&redlink=1 "Hangzhou Flower Nursery (page does not exist)") and [Hangzhou Botanical Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_Botanical_Garden "Hangzhou Botanical Garden") showcase a diverse array of flowers and plants. In the southwest, Taiziwan Park and Huagang Park draw visitors in spring with colorful tulips and seasonal blossoms. On the southeastern shore, Liulangwenying Park and Changqiao Park offer scenic views and spaces for relaxation.

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Hangzhou_%2815730606661%29.jpg/250px-Hangzhou_%2815730606661%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hangzhou_(15730606661).jpg)

[Changqiao Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changqiao_Park?action=edit&redlink=1 "Changqiao Park (page does not exist)")

Around West Lake, several historic private gardens have been preserved. Liu Villa, on the northwest shore, was originally a private Qing-dynasty garden reflecting classic Chinese landscape design. Today, it serves as the West Lake State Guest House, a luxury hotel known for hosting important events and guests. Wang Villa, on the southwestern corner of the lake, was also built during the Qing dynasty and has since been restored as part of Xizi Hotel. Jiang Villa, on the eastern shore near the Lakeside area, now operates as the Lakeside Tea House. Guo Villa, located on the northwestern shore at the foot of Gushan near Qixia Ridge, is one of Hangzhou's best-preserved Qing-dynasty gardens and is open to the public as a government-run park.

### Modern architecture

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Modern architecture")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/%E8%A5%BF%E6%B9%96%E5%8D%9A%E7%89%A9%E9%A6%86.jpg/250px-%E8%A5%BF%E6%B9%96%E5%8D%9A%E7%89%A9%E9%A6%86.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:西湖博物馆.jpg)

[West Lake Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Lake_Museum "West Lake Museum")

See also: [Hangzhou historic houses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_historic_houses "Hangzhou historic houses")

West Lake is home to many Western-style residences constructed during the Republic of China era (1911–1949). On Gushan, notable sites include the Memorial Pavilion to Sun Yat-sen, the former residences of Du Yuesheng and Chiang Kai-shek, as well as Yiyunji Lu Villa. Along Beishan Road, significant landmarks feature the Former Residence of Chiang Ching-kuo and various villas such as Run Lu, Ru Lu, Xing Lu, and Baoqing, in addition to notable hotels like Hangzhou Hotel, Xinxin Hotel, and Qiushui Villa. The eastern shore also hosts historic structures including Shihan Jingshe Villa, Long Bridge Villa, Guo Villa, and the former residence of Huang Fu. Modern architecture complements these historical sites, with buildings such as the West Lake Museum and a range of luxury hotels like the Grand Hyatt Hangzhou, upscale shopping centers, such as the Hubin Yintai in77 complex.

## Hydrology

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Hydrology")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedi
evidence.title: West Lake - Wikipedia

evidence.text:
a.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/China_Hangzhou_Nine_Greeks_Meandering_Through_a_Misty_Forest.JPG/250px-China_Hangzhou_Nine_Greeks_Meandering_Through_a_Misty_Forest.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:China_Hangzhou_Nine_Greeks_Meandering_Through_a_Misty_Forest.JPG)

Misty Trees by Nine Streams

With a catchment area spanning 21.22 square kilometers, the lake supports an annual runoff and storage volume of about 14 million cubic meters each. The lake draws around 120 million cubic meters of water annually from the Qiantang River. Natural inflows come from the Jinsha, Longhong, Qishan (also known as Huiyin), and Changqiao streams. The lake's water level is maintained at a consistent Yellow Sea reference level of 7.15 meters, fluctuating by only ±0.05 meters. Seasonal water levels range from a high of 7.70 meters to a low of 6.92 meters, with a variation of approximately 50 centimeters. With a storage capacity of about 14.3 million cubic meters, the lake averages 2.27 meters in depth, reaching a maximum of 5 meters and a minimum of less than 1 meter. Average annual precipitation directly over the lake amounts to 5.63 million cubic meters, while the lake's water system has a scour coefficient of 1.49. During dry seasons, when the reservoir gate is closed, the flow rate drops to zero, and even during the flood season, it rarely exceeds 0.05 m/s.[[72]](#cite_note-72)

Located on the southeastern edge of China's hilly regions and the northern boundary of the subtropical zone, West Lake receives an annual solar radiation of 100–110 kcal/cm2 and enjoys 1,800–2,100 sunshine hours per year.[[73]](#cite_note-73) Due to Hangzhou's mild climate, West Lake seldom freezes during winter. The last complete freezing of the lake occurred in January 1977, when the city experienced extreme cold, with temperatures plunging to a record low of −8.6 °C. Partial and temporary freezing, however, is observed almost annually, contingent on weather conditions.[[74]](#cite_note-74)

## Flora

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Flora")]

West Lake is surrounded by rich and varied vegetation. Within the nominated area, there are 1,369 species of spermatophytes from 739 genera in 184 families, including 28 gymnosperm species from 19 genera in 7 families and 1,273 angiosperm species from 675 genera in 150 families. Additionally, there are 68 species of pteridophytes from 45 genera in 27 families.[[75]](#cite_note-:23-75)

### Seasonal flowers

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Seasonal flowers")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/%E8%A5%BF%E6%B9%96._%E5%B2%B3%E6%B9%96-%E7%8E%89%E5%B8%A6%E6%A1%A5_-_panoramio.jpg/250px-%E8%A5%BF%E6%B9%96._%E5%B2%B3%E6%B9%96-%E7%8E%89%E5%B8%A6%E6%A1%A5_-_panoramio.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:西湖._岳湖-玉带桥_-_panoramio.jpg)

Lotus Flowers upon the Yuehu Lake

The four main seasonal flowers of the West Lake landscape—[peach blossoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peach "Peach"), [lotus flowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelumbo_nucifera "Nelumbo nucifera"), [osmanthus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osmanthus "Osmanthus"), and [plum blossoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prunus_mume "Prunus mume")—are closely connected to Hangzhou's cultural heritage such as the [Ten Scenes of West Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten_Scenes_of_West_Lake "Ten Scenes of West Lake"). These plants embody the concept of integrating seasonal beauty into the landscape design of these scenic areas.[[76]](#cite_note-:24-76)

* Peach trees and willows line the shores and causeways, adding colour to the lake during spring and early summer. On the Su and Bai Causeways, one willow are typically intercropped with one peach, a pattern designed by Su Shi in the 11th century.[[76]](#cite_note-:24-76)

Lotus flowers are grown in 14 designated areas covering around 20 hectares, primarily found in the North Inner Lake and Yuehu Lake.[[76]](#cite_note-:24-76)
* Osmanthus trees are widely planted throughout the gardens along the banks of the lake, with Manjuelong and the Hangzhou Botanical Garden being the most notable spots for their dense plantings and fragrant blooms in autumn.[[76]](#cite_note-:24-76)
* The plum blossom, which represents steadfastness and purity in Chinese culture, are grown in Lingfeng Hill, Gushan Hill, and the Xixi Stream.[[76]](#cite_note-:24-76)

### [Longjing tea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longjing_tea "Longjing tea")

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Longjing tea")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/%E9%BE%99%E4%BA%95%E6%9D%91%E8%8C%B6%E5%9B%AD.jpg/250px-%E9%BE%99%E4%BA%95%E6%9D%91%E8%8C%B6%E5%9B%AD.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:龙井村茶园.jpg)

Tea Plantation at Longjing

The [Longjing Tea Plantation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longjing_Tea_Fields "Longjing Tea Fields") is nestled in the hills to the west of West Lake and is renowned for producing Longjing tea, a variety that thrives due to the unique geographical conditions of the area. The tea plants are cultivated on the slopes of these hills, arranged on curved or open terraces near brooks in neatly organised plots. This region benefits from a monsoonal humid climate typical of the northern subtropical zone, characterised by distinct seasons, adequate rainfall, and year-round moisture. The plantation's micro-climate, influenced by its location between the Qiantang River to the north and the Jiuxi Streams to the south, creates a foggy and misty environment ideal for tea growth, especially in spring. The surrounding hills, such as Tianzhu Hill and Beigao Peak, protect the area from cold winds, while the valley leading to the Qiantang River draws in humid air, maintaining a warm, wet climate.[[76]](#cite_note-:24-76)

### Ancient trees

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Ancient trees")]

The area around West Lake also features numerous ancient and rare trees, many associated with historic temples and monasteries such as Lingyin Temple and Tianzhu Temple, as well as Wushan and Gushan Hills. Among these, 125 trees from 22 species are over 300 years old, serving as living records of the region's ecological history.[[75]](#cite_note-:23-75)

## Economy

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Economy")]

According to the Hangzhou Statistical Bureau, in 2017, the West Lake Scenic Area recorded a [gross regional product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_regional_product "Gross regional product") of 112.11 billion yuan (approximately 16.70 billion US dollars). The services sector contributed around 90% of this figure, while manufacturing accounted for roughly 10%, and agriculture contributed less than 0.1%. The GDP per capita for the region was 136,330 yuan (approximately 20,302 US dollars).[[77]](#cite_note-77)

### Tourism

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Tourism")]

Recognised as a National Key Scenic Resort in 1982 and designated a [national AAAAA tourist destination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AAAAA_Tourist_Attractions_of_China "AAAAA Tourist Attractions of China") in 2006, the West Lake Scenic Area is one of China's most popular tourist attractions and a significant cultural landmark.[[78]](#cite_note-:11-78) In 2002, the municipal government removed the park walls, allowing free access
evidence.title: West Lake - Wikipedia

evidence.text:
to most areas around the lake. This made West Lake the first major tourist destination to eliminate admission fees, with the aim of boosting the sales of nearby restaurants, hotels, and retail stores.[[12]](#cite_note-:20-12)

Despite most scenic spots around the lake being free, the non-free scenic spots within the scenic area include [Hangzhou Zoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_Zoo "Hangzhou Zoo"), [Hangzhou Botanical Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_Botanical_Garden "Hangzhou Botanical Garden"), Mulan Mountain Tea Garden, Feilai Peak Scenic Area (with [Lingyin Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingyin_Temple "Lingyin Temple") inside), Guo Villa, [Yue Fei Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yue_Fei_Temple "Yue Fei Temple"), Yellow Dragon Cave, [Liuhe Pagoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liuhe_Pagoda "Liuhe Pagoda") Park, [Galloping Tiger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreaming_of_the_Tiger_Spring "Dreaming of the Tiger Spring") Park, Bamboo-Lined Path at Yunqi, [City God Pavilion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_God_Pavilion_of_Hangzhou?action=edit&redlink=1 "City God Pavilion of Hangzhou (page does not exist)"), [Wansong Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wansong_Academy?action=edit&redlink=1 "Wansong Academy (page does not exist)"), [Children's Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children's_Park_(Hangzhou)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Children's Park (Hangzhou) (page does not exist)"), the [Former Residence of Hu Xueyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Former_Residence_of_Hu_Xueyan "Former Residence of Hu Xueyan") and the [Leifeng Pagoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leifeng_Pagoda "Leifeng Pagoda").

Each year, the scenic area receive more than 30 million visitors.[[79]](#cite_note-:25-79) During public holidays, West Lake is one of the most crowded scenic spots in China.[[80]](#cite_note-80)[[81]](#cite_note-81)[[82]](#cite_note-82) During the 2024 National Day holiday, the area recorded 4.426 million visitors over seven days, representing a 30.92% increase compared to the previous year.[[14]](#cite_note-:21-14) Following the free-access policy, the income of the scenic area increased substantially, from 29.4 billion yuan in 2002 to 400.5 billion yuan in 2019.[[83]](#cite_note-83) This strategic move contributed to the area's economic resilience during the [2008 financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis "2008 financial crisis") and the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") by reducing dependence on admission fees as a primary source of income.[[12]](#cite_note-:20-12)

### Agriculture

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Agriculture")]

Historically, the lake needs to strike a balance between aquaculture and irrigation. By the 6th century, West Lake became an irrigation source, supported by a network of canals aiding rice cultivation. From the 7th century, it provided local residents with fish, aquatic animals (e.g., snails, crabs), and both wild and cultivated plants (e.g., water chestnuts, wild rice shoots), which inspired local cuisine. Absence of intensive management from the government, as seen in the Yuan and Republican era, often led to extensive aquaculture of the lake, while periodic dredging to maintain its irrigation function also temporarily affected habitats and reduced plant food sources. In the 1980s, the annual fish yield peaked at approximately 400 tons but was later reduced to around 250 tons due to regulatory measures aimed at improving water quality.[[79]](#cite_note-:25-79)

The [Longjing Tea Plantation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longjing,_Hangzhou "Longjing, Hangzhou"), situated in the hills west of West Lake, has been a cornerstone of Chinese tea culture for centuries.[[76]](#cite_note-:24-76) Longjing tea, a renowned variety of Chinese green tea, is produced from fresh, non-fermented leaves native to West Lake area.[[84]](#cite_note-84) Before the

anti-corruption movement led by Xi Jinping in 2014, Longjing tea was highly valued and often gifted, at times even surpassing the price of gold.[[85]](#cite_note-85) In 2019, the core West Lake production area yielded 502.35 tons, generating a revenue of 3.22 billion yuan (approximately 465.57 million US dollars).[[86]](#cite_note-86)

### Gastronomy

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: Gastronomy")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/West_Lake_Fish_in_Vinegar_Gravy.jpg/250px-West_Lake_Fish_in_Vinegar_Gravy.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:West_Lake_Fish_in_Vinegar_Gravy.jpg)

[West Lake Fish in Vinegar Gravy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Lake_Fish_in_Vinegar_Gravy "West Lake Fish in Vinegar Gravy")

[Zhejiang cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_cuisine "Zhejiang cuisine"), one of the [eight traditional cuisines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eight_Cuisines_of_China "Eight Cuisines of China") of China,[[87]](#cite_note-87) is renowned for its light, mild flavours with a hint of sweetness.[[88]](#cite_note-:19-88) Thanks to its geographical location, which provides access to an abundance of seasonal ingredients, Hangzhou's branch of Zhejiang cuisine is divided into two main types: lake cuisine and city cuisine.[[88]](#cite_note-:19-88) Historically, these types catered to distinguished officials and the broader population, respectively. Lake cuisine emphasises fish, shrimp, and vegetables, while city cuisine uses more commonly available local meats.[[89]](#cite_note-89) Signature dishes made from West Lake's freshwater fish and lotus root include [West Lake Fish in Vinegar Gravy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Lake_Fish_in_Vinegar_Gravy "West Lake Fish in Vinegar Gravy") and [Beggar's Chicken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beggar's_chicken "Beggar's chicken").[[88]](#cite_note-:19-88) However, despite its rich tradition, Hangzhou's local cuisine faces declining popularity among younger generations. This is attributed to limited options that effectively balance price and taste, earning the city a reputation as a "food desert."[[90]](#cite_note-90)

## Culture

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Culture")]

A Trip to Lake Abundant

> I've never traveled to Hangzhou's West Lake  
>  But seem to have met it in my dreams someplace:  
>  A vague and indistinct expanse of water and clouds  
>  Where lotus leaves merge with weeping-willow branches.

— [Huang Zunxian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huang_Zunxian "Huang Zunxian") (1848–1905), translation by Jerry Dean Schmidt[[91]](#cite_note-91)

### Garden designs

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Garden designs")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/%E6%97%A5%E4%B8%AD%E5%8F%8B%E5%A5%BD%E5%BA%AD%E5%9C%92_%28%E5%B2%90%E9%98%9C%E5%B8%82%29Gifukoen014.jpg/250px-%E6%97%A5%E4%B8%AD%E5%8F%8B%E5%A5%BD%E5%BA%AD%E5%9C%92_%28%E5%B2%90%E9%98%9C%E5%B8%82%29Gifukoen014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:日中友好庭園_(岐阜市)Gifukoen014.jpg)

The West Lake as replicated in miniature size in the Japan-China Friendship Garden, [Gifu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gifu "Gifu")

A human-made landscape,[[92]](#cite_note-92) West Lake exemplifies Chinese landscape aesthetics, symbolising harmony between humans and nature as well as the projection of human emotions onto natural scenery. The poetic names create framed views of scenery to be seen from specific locations.[[93]](#cite_note-:18-93) West Lake landscape embodies six key elements inspired by Chinese literature:[[3]](#cite_note-:14-3)

* Natural hills and waters;
* A spatial arrangement with hills on three sides and the city on the fourth;
* A layout featuring two causeways and three isles;
* The tradition of poetic names fo

evidence.text:
r scenic spots;
* Historic monuments and sites;
* Distinctive flora.

Since the Song dynasty, people imitated the views of West Lake in their private gardens, borrowing one or more features of the lake. Such examples include [Kunming Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunming_Lake "Kunming Lake") and the West Causeway at the [Summer Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Palace "Summer Palace") in [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing "Beijing"), the Lower Lake at the [Summer Retreat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chengde_Mountain_Resort "Chengde Mountain Resort") in [Rehe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chengde "Chengde"), the poetic place names at the [Kyu Shiba Rikyu Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyu_Shiba_Rikyu_Garden "Kyu Shiba Rikyu Garden") and [Koishikawa Kōrakuen Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koishikawa_Kōrakuen_Garden "Koishikawa Kōrakuen Garden") in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"), Japan.[[93]](#cite_note-:18-93) [Kintaikyo Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kintai_Bridge "Kintai Bridge") in Iwakuni, Japan was inspired by bridges over Hangzhou's West Lake.[[94]](#cite_note-94) In 1989, [Japan-China Friendship Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan-China_Friendship_Garden?action=edit&redlink=1 "Japan-China Friendship Garden (page does not exist)"), which involves a miniature replica of West Lake, was built inside the [Gifu Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gifu_Park "Gifu Park") in [Gifu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gifu,_Gifu "Gifu, Gifu"), Japan, in memory of the city's friendly tie with Hangzhou since 1979.[[95]](#cite_note-95)

### Fine arts

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Fine arts")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/ab/West_Lake_on_RMB.jpg/250px-West_Lake_on_RMB.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:West_Lake_on_RMB.jpg)

Three Ponds Mirroring the Moon on the Chinese banknote

For centuries, West Lake has also been a prominent theme in [East Asian landscape painting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_landscape_painting "Chinese landscape painting"),[[78]](#cite_note-:11-78) even though many painters may have never seen the lake in person.[[96]](#cite_note-:12-96) The [State Administration of Cultural Heritage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Cultural_Heritage_Administration "National Cultural Heritage Administration") (2011) listed more than 500 paintings and calligraphic works that feature West Lake since the Tang dynasty (618–907),[[97]](#cite_note-97) while Japanese paintings of the lake may even outnumber the existing Chinese depictions.[[96]](#cite_note-:12-96) In 1928, the [National Academy of Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Academy_of_Art "China Academy of Art") was founded by the lake as the country's first higher education institution in art.[[98]](#cite_note-98) As a cultural icon of China, it has been featured on [Chinese currency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renminbi "Renminbi"), including the one-yuan [banknote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banknote "Banknote") in the 1979 [Bank of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_China "Bank of China") [Foreign Exchange Certificate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_exchange_certificate "Foreign exchange certificate")[[7]](#cite_note-:28-7) and the [2005 Renminbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_series_of_the_renminbi "Fifth series of the renminbi"),[[8]](#cite_note-:29-8) as well as in the [Chinese passport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_passport "Chinese passport").[[9]](#cite_note-:30-9)

### Popular culture

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Popular culture")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/%E6%B8%B8%E6%B9%96_20231026.jpg/250px-%E6%B8%B8%E6%B9%96_20231026.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:游湖_20231026.jpg)

The scene of Yun opera *[The Legend of the White Snake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_the_White_Snake "Legend of the White Snake"),* where the hero and heroine first met over West Lake

West Lake has deeply influenced Chinese literature, inspiring poets and writers for centuries. Works by poets such as [Bai Juyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bai_Juyi "Bai Juyi"), [Su Shi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Su_Shi "Su Shi"), [Xu Zhimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xu_Zhimo "Xu Zhimo"), and [Hu Shih](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hu_Shih "Hu Shih") celebrate its historic sites and natural beauty. The Ming essayist Zhang Dai also honoured the lake in his writings, including *[Reminiscence and Dream of Tao'an](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_Memories_of_Tao’an "Dream Memories of Tao’an")* and *[Search for West Lake in Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_for_West_Lake_in_Dreams?action=edit&redlink=1 "Search for West Lake in Dreams (page does not exist)").* In folklore, West Lake serves as the setting for several popular tales, including *[The Legend of the White Snake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend_of_the_White_Snake "Legend of the White Snake")*,[[114]](#cite_note-114)[[115]](#cite_note-:13-115) the stories of [Ji Gong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ji_Gong "Ji Gong"),[[116]](#cite_note-116)[[115]](#cite_note-:13-115) and *[Butterfly Lovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butterfly_Lovers "Butterfly Lovers")*.[[117]](#cite_note-117)[[115]](#cite_note-:13-115)

During the 1920s and 1930s, West Lake was a prominent theme in popular film music. The Cantonese songwriter [Lü Wencheng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lü_Wencheng "Lü Wencheng") composed the classic *[Autumn Moon Over the Calm Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autumn_Moon_Over_the_Calm_Lake "Autumn Moon Over the Calm Lake")* and *Three Ponds Mirroring the Moon* during his 1930s visit, while Tan Peiyun contributed *Listening to Orioles at Willow Waves*. These compositions are now considered staples of Cantonese music. The 1959 violin concerto *Butterfly Lovers*, inspired by the Yue Opera adaptation, remains a celebrated piece in Chinese orchestral repertoire. Between 2004 and 2008, Wang Guoping compiled \*The Wes
evidence.title: West Lake - Wikipedia

evidence.text:
t Lake Series\*, which includes the extensive *Collection of Documents about West Lake* (30 volumes) and *The Complete Library of West Lake* (50 volumes).

The influence of West Lake extends to film and performance. The 2005 Hong Kong film *[A West Lake Moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_West_Lake_Moment "A West Lake Moment")*, directed by [Yim Ho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yim_Ho "Yim Ho") and Yang Zi. Since 2006, the Hangzhou Art Week has been rebranded as the Spring of West Lake Art Festival. In 2007, director [Zhang Yimou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Yimou "Zhang Yimou") launched *Impression West Lake*, a popular and ongoing lakeside performance. Additionally, the West Lake International Documentary Festival, initiated in 2017, has become a significant event in China's film scene.

### Toponymy

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=West_Lake&action=edit&section=34 "Edit section: Toponymy")]

The following places are named after or associated with West Lake:

* Administrative division: Xihu Subdistrict, [Xihu District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xihu,_Hangzhou "Xihu, Hangzhou"), Hubin Subdistrict
* Roads: Xihu Avenue, Hubin Road, [Hubin Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubin_Park?action=edit&redlink=1 "Hubin Park (page does not exist)"), West Lake Tunnel
* Schools: West Lake Primary School, Hangzhou West Lake Senior High School, Hangzhou West Lake Vocational High School, [Westlake University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westlake_University "Westlake University")
* Buildings: [West Lake Cultural Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Lake_Cultural_Square "West Lake Cultural Square"), [West Lake Cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Lake_Cinema?action=edit&redlink=1 "West Lake Cinema (page does not exist)"), [West Lake Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Lake_Museum "West Lake Museum"), West Lake State Guest House, Xizi Hotel
* Lakes: [Slender West Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slender_West_Lake "Slender West Lake") of Yangzhou, [West Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Lake_(Huizhou) "West Lake (Huizhou)") of [Huizhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huizhou "Huizhou")[[118]](#cite_note-118)
* Festivals: West Lake International Documentary Festival, West Lake Day

# Ancient Chinese cultural landscape, the West Lake of Hangzhou, inscribed on UNESCO’s World Heritage List

![](https://whc.unesco.org/uploads/thumbs/news_767-500-292-20110624220310.webp)

The World Heritage Committee has inscribed the West Lake Cultural Landscape of Hangzhou, comprising the West Lake and the hills surrounding its three sides, on UNESCO’s World Heritage List.

The inscribed landscape has inspired famous poets, scholars and artists since the 9th century. It comprises numerous temples, pagodas, pavilions, gardens and ornamental trees, as well as causeways and artificial islands.   
 These additions have been made to improve the landscape west of the city of Hangzhou to the south of the Yangtze river.  
   
 The West Lake has influenced garden design in the rest of China as well as Japan and Korea over the centuries and bears an exceptional testimony to the cultural tradition of improving landscapes to create a series of vistas reflecting an idealised fusion between humans and nature.  
   
 A total of 35 nominations, including natural, cultural and mixed properties are being reviewed by the Committee, which is holding its 35th session at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris. The session will end on 29 June.

# West Lake Cultural Landscape - UNESCO World Heritage Site
## Channel: World Heritage Journey
9.68K subscribers
18 likes

### Description
1,636 views
Posted: 2019-12-06
West Lake Cultural Landscape is a beautiful and impressive UNESCO World Heritage site, located in the city of Hangzhou in eastern China. This large lake has inspired many Chinese painters, poets, scholars and other artists for centuries, and it certainly inspired us as well! We spent an entire day walking around the lake, exploring the various famed scenes at different points, and soaking in the atmosphere. Let's check it out!
